long_biography.plain_text:
Jerome Fisher grew up in a Boston shoe manufacturing family, worked in his father’s factories and studied industrial engineering at Wharton. An early venture failed, but work with Sumitomo took him into Brazilian production and introduced him to Vince Camuto. Together they created a business built around translating high fashion into accessible footwear.

Nine West developed from that sourcing model into a major wholesale and retail group, adding brands and stores before going public. Its sale to Jones Apparel made Fisher chairman emeritus and ended his daily operating role. He then devoted more time to education and philanthropy, endowing Penn’s management and technology program, supporting the restoration of its Fine Arts Library and contributing to medical and cultural institutions.
